svg.title: RunAll call sequence for the dynamic Stromgren photoheating example
svg.desc: A vertical call-sequence diagram showing the main startup path, the RunAll startup chain, the output-time driver, and the postprocessing steps.
svg.text: RunAll() call sequence
Dynamic Stromgren Sphere Photoheating 1D
1. main()
Load YAML, create output directories, write the IC snapshot.
2. Rsim(runparams)
Build Par, Mesh, Fluid, Solver, and EOS objects.
3. RunAll(outputtime=0)
Enter the IC-driven startup path for the dynamic example.
4. Callreadhdf5()
Read InitialCondition.hdf5, validate dimensions, and set the start time.
rio.readhdf5() + checkparams() + Fluid.SetFluidTime()
5. SetMesh()
Rebuild mesh geometry and ghost cells from the IC state.
6. SetFluid()
Initialize the fluid ghost cells and pressure from the IC state.
7. SetInitFluid()
Convert runtime parameters to code units, then populate the initial
conserved state and apply the first radiative-transfer sweep.
ConvertParametersToCodeUnits() -> Solver.SetBoundary() -> Solver.SetConserved() -> Solver.ApplyRadiativeTransfer()
8. Run()
Write used_parameters.yaml, then follow the output-time branch.
This example has outputtimefilename, so Run() dispatches to run_with_output_times().
9. run_with_output_times()
Write output 0, step with Rsim.Step(), and write snapshots at target times.
Step() -> hydro update -> chemistry / radiation source update -> next step
Postprocessing: load saved outputs, reconstruct the final state, and save the profile and front plots.
